catalogue: Australian structural concrete, reinforcement, prestressing, precast and formwork

objects.name: cementitious binder
objects.definition: The finely divided reactive material in a concrete mix that combines with water and binds the aggregates into hardened concrete.
functions: Bind aggregate particles
Develop the cement paste matrix
Carry selected cement and supplementary-material composition

cad.placement: Dispersed through the concrete mix rather than drawn as a separate layer after hardening

notes: Cementitious binder is useful for specifications and quantities; ordinary member geometry should normally show the resulting concrete composite, not individual binder grains.

objects.name: general purpose cement
objects.definition: A manufactured hydraulic cement powder used as the principal reactive binder in general concrete, mortar and grout mixes.
functions: React with water
Bind aggregates
Provide the principal cement component of a selected mix

cad.placement: Within the cementitious binder portion of a concrete mix

notes: GP is an Australian product designation; do not convert it automatically to a proprietary mix or a structural strength grade.

objects.name: blended cement
objects.definition: A manufactured cement in which Portland cement clinker is combined with selected mineral components to form one supplied binder product.
functions: Provide a factory-blended hydraulic binder
Combine cement and selected mineral components
Contribute to fresh and hardened concrete properties

cad.placement: Within the binder portion of a concrete mix

notes: A factory blended cement and a concrete producer's combination of separate binder materials can reach similar compositions but are not the same supply object.

objects.name: supplementary cementitious material
objects.definition: A finely divided mineral material used with cement to contribute to the binder system and alter selected fresh, hardened or durability properties of concrete.
functions: Supplement the principal cement
Participate in or modify the binder reaction
Support a documented concrete mix composition

cad.placement: Dispersed through the binder portion of the concrete

notes: The material family is stored for specification and embodied-impact work; it is not normally separate completed geometry.

objects.name: fly ash for concrete
objects.definition: A fine ash product selected as a supplementary cementitious material in a concrete binder system.
functions: Supplement cement
Contribute to the documented binder composition
Modify selected concrete properties when properly specified

cad.placement: Dispersed in the cementitious binder

notes: The ontology records the selected conforming material, not every ash stream from a power station.

objects.name: ground granulated blast-furnace slag for concrete
objects.definition: Finely ground granulated blast-furnace slag selected as a supplementary cementitious material in a concrete binder system.
functions: Supplement cement
Contribute latent hydraulic binder material
Modify the selected concrete mix properties

cad.placement: Dispersed in the cementitious binder

notes: Do not infer slag content or proportion from concrete colour.

objects.name: silica fume for concrete
objects.definition: A very fine amorphous silica material selected in controlled quantity as part of a concrete binder system.
functions: Supplement the binder
Contribute reactive fine material
Support documented high-performance or durability properties

cad.placement: Dispersed in the cementitious binder

notes: Its presence and dose are evidence-backed mix attributes, never an inference from surface smoothness.

objects.name: concrete mixing water
objects.definition: Water deliberately included in a concrete batch to hydrate the binder and provide the workability needed for mixing and placement.
functions: Hydrate cementitious binder
Enable mixing and placement
Contribute to the specified water-to-binder relationship

cad.placement: Dispersed through fresh concrete and chemically or physically incorporated during hardening

notes: Do not draw a separate water layer in hardened concrete; store it as mix data.

objects.name: fine concrete aggregate
objects.definition: The smaller graded aggregate particles used with binder, water and coarse aggregate to form the concrete composite.
functions: Fill the concrete particle skeleton
Contribute to workability and hardened volume
Transfer stress within the composite matrix

cad.pattern: Distributed particles represented by material data rather than individual geometry at ordinary scale
cad.placement: Within the hardened concrete matrix

notes: Individual particles may be procedurally textured for a close-up visualisation but must not become thousands of structural objects.

objects.name: coarse concrete aggregate
objects.definition: The larger graded aggregate particles forming much of the solid skeleton and volume of ordinary concrete.
functions: Form the coarse particle skeleton
Contribute bulk and dimensional stability
Transfer stress through the hardened composite

cad.pattern: Distributed particles represented by material data at ordinary building scale
cad.placement: Within the hardened concrete matrix

notes: Aggregate size affects detailing around reinforcement and pumping but must come from the selected mix, not a default texture.

objects.name: chemical concrete admixture
objects.definition: A controlled chemical ingredient added in relatively small quantity during batching to modify selected fresh or hardened properties of concrete.
functions: Modify a documented concrete property
Support placement or performance of the selected mix
Remain recorded as part of batch composition

cad.placement: Dispersed through the concrete batch
cad.load: Mix constituent rather than a separate hardened layer

notes: Marketing labels such as waterproofing admixture do not allow the tool to infer a watertight structure without the complete design and evidence.

objects.name: discrete concrete fibre reinforcement
objects.definition: Short separate fibres distributed through a concrete mix to provide a documented crack-control, toughness or residual-strength role.
functions: Distribute reinforcement through the concrete matrix
Bridge small cracks where designed
Provide selected post-cracking or crack-control behaviour

cad.pattern: Statistical three-dimensional distribution rather than individually placed bars
cad.placement: Within the concrete matrix
cad.load: Only the documented fibre role is structural

notes: At ordinary model scale store fibres as a material attribute; generate explicit strands only for explanatory close-ups.

objects.name: cast-in-place concrete structural system
objects.definition: A structural arrangement whose concrete members are formed, reinforced where required and cast in their final building positions.
functions: Combine concrete members into a load path
Coordinate reinforcement, joints, embeds and openings
Transfer actions to the supporting structure and foundations

ncc_references.relationship: Provides the structural performance and Deemed-to-Satisfy route context for concrete construction outside the limited prescriptive Housing Provisions footing-and-slab scope.

cad.pattern: Connected member network divided by real construction and movement joints
cad.placement: At final building position
cad.end: Roof, upper support or member termination
cad.opening: All designed penetrations, blockouts and recesses remain explicit
cad.load: Primary structural system when designed as such

notes: A shape generator must not select member sizes, reinforcement, prestress or joint locations without project design inputs.

objects.name: plain concrete element
objects.definition: A concrete member whose structural behaviour is not assigned to conventional embedded steel reinforcement or prestressing tendons.
functions: Provide a concrete mass or member
Carry only the actions permitted by its documented design
Form durable permanent geometry

cad.placement: At the documented permanent member location
cad.opening: Documented openings only

notes: Absence of modelled bars is not proof that an element was designed as plain concrete; missing reinforcement data must stay unknown.

objects.name: reinforced concrete element
objects.definition: A permanent concrete member and its embedded steel reinforcement acting together in the completed structure.
functions: Combine concrete compression and reinforcement resistance
Carry the element's documented actions
Control cracking and provide ductility where designed

cad.pattern: Concrete volume containing an independently selectable reinforcement topology
cad.placement: At final member position
cad.opening: Reinforcement and concrete coordinate around every opening
cad.load: Primary or secondary structural element as designed

notes: Concrete and reinforcement remain separate selectable objects even though they act compositely.

objects.name: prestressed concrete element
objects.definition: A concrete element containing high-strength tendons that introduce a deliberate compressive stress before the element carries its full service actions.
functions: Use tendon force to precompress concrete
Control service cracking and deflection where designed
Carry actions through concrete, tendons and anchor or bond zones
attributes: concrete age at stressing or transfer

cad.pattern: Concrete member with explicit tendon paths and end or transfer zones
cad.placement: Cast in place or prefabricated according to method
cad.opening: Openings require coordinated tendon deviation or exclusion zones
cad.load: Prestressed structural element only when designed

notes: Prestressed is the broad family; pre-tensioned and post-tensioned describe different ways force is introduced.

objects.name: post-tensioned concrete element
objects.definition: A prestressed concrete element whose tendons are tensioned against the hardened concrete after it has reached the required condition.
functions: Introduce compressive force after concrete hardens
Span or control service behaviour as designed
Transfer tendon force through permanent anchorages
materials: duct and grout or monostrand sheathing

cad.pattern: Member volume containing curved or straight tendon runs
cad.placement: At final structural position
cad.opening: Tendon exclusion and deviation geometry remains explicit

notes: The strand path is drawable; prestressing force, losses and acceptance are versioned design and construction evidence.

objects.name: reinforced concrete frame
objects.definition: A connected structural frame of reinforced concrete columns, beams, walls or slabs whose joints and members form the primary load path.
functions: Carry vertical and lateral actions
Connect floor and roof systems to foundations
Provide a durable structural skeleton

cad.pattern: Column, beam, wall and slab network on a structural grid
cad.placement: From foundations through supported storeys
cad.opening: Building and service openings coordinated with members

notes: Do not infer moment, braced or wall-frame behaviour simply from members touching in the model.

objects.name: structural concrete slab system
objects.definition: A structural concrete plate or ribbed floor system that distributes loads to beams, walls, columns or the ground according to its documented support arrangement.
functions: Form a structural floor or roof plane
Distribute imposed and permanent actions
Coordinate openings, setdowns, toppings and edge details

cad.pattern: Continuous or jointed plate field over documented supports
cad.placement: At structural floor or roof level
cad.start: First support line or slab edge
cad.opening: Penetrations, shafts, setdowns and recesses remain explicit

notes: This parent covers ground-supported and suspended families; use the existing concrete-foundations catalogue for slab-on-ground anatomy.

objects.name: suspended concrete floor system
objects.definition: A concrete floor or roof slab system spanning between discrete supports with occupied, service or open space beneath it.
functions: Span between beams, walls or columns
Carry floor or roof actions
Provide diaphragm and fire-separating roles where designed

cad.pattern: Floor plate spanning over discrete support lines or points
cad.placement: Above a lower storey, subfloor or open space
cad.opening: Shafts, stairs and penetrations require local structural coordination

notes: A suspended waffle slab is not the same assembly as a ground-supported waffle raft despite similar underside patterns.

objects.name: one-way concrete slab
objects.definition: A suspended slab arranged to span mainly in one direction between approximately parallel support lines.
functions: Carry plate actions mainly across one span direction
Transfer loads to parallel supports
Form the structural floor field

cad.pattern: Repeated primary reinforcement or tendon runs across the short or designed span
cad.placement: Between parallel beams or walls
cad.opening: Openings interrupt the load field and require designed trimming

notes: Aspect ratio alone must not be the only rule for declaring structural span direction.

objects.name: two-way concrete slab
objects.definition: A suspended slab arranged to distribute significant plate actions in two directions to supporting beams, walls or columns.
functions: Carry loads in two principal directions
Distribute actions to surrounding or point supports
Form the structural floor field
attributes: column strips and middle strips where used

cad.pattern: Orthogonal or documented two-direction reinforcement fields
cad.placement: Over perimeter, line or point supports
cad.start: Slab boundary or support grid origin
cad.opening: Openings require explicit trimming and support-zone checks

notes: The tool may show support topology but cannot determine punching capacity from visible geometry alone.

objects.name: flat plate concrete slab
objects.definition: A substantially uniform-depth suspended slab supported directly by columns without downstand beams, drop panels or column capitals at the support zones.
functions: Provide a flat soffit
Transfer slab actions directly to columns
Create an unobstructed service zone below the slab

cad.pattern: Uniform soffit across a point-support grid
cad.placement: Directly on columns or column heads without drops
cad.opening: Keep openings clear of documented support zones unless designed

notes: A visually flat soffit does not prove the system is a flat plate; hidden beams or thickening must remain possible until documented.

objects.name: flat slab with support thickenings
objects.definition: A column-supported concrete slab system using drop panels, column capitals or both to thicken and spread the support zones while retaining broad flat soffit fields between them.
functions: Transfer two-way slab actions to columns
Increase depth or bearing geometry near supports
Reduce or avoid continuous downstand beams

cad.pattern: Slab field with repeated local support-zone thickenings
cad.placement: Over a column grid
cad.opening: Openings coordinate with support thickenings and tendons or bars

notes: Australian and international usage can blur flat slab and flat plate; the catalogue keeps the physical presence of support thickenings explicit.

objects.name: concrete slab drop panel
objects.definition: A local slab thickening extending around a column or point support below the main soffit of a flat slab.
functions: Increase structural depth near a support
Spread support-zone actions
Provide local punching and flexural geometry where designed

cad.pattern: Repeated local thickened plates at selected supports
cad.placement: Below the main slab soffit around a column
cad.opening: Avoid uncoordinated openings through the drop
cad.load: Part of the slab support zone

notes: A setdown is a top-surface depression; a drop panel projects below the main soffit.

objects.name: concrete column capital
objects.definition: A flared or enlarged concrete head at the top of a column that spreads the interface between the column and a supported slab.
functions: Enlarge the column-to-slab support zone
Transfer actions between slab and column
Provide local structural geometry where designed

cad.pattern: Repeated at selected column heads
cad.placement: Between column shaft and slab or drop panel
cad.opening: No opening unless specifically coordinated

notes: A capital belongs to the support geometry, not to the architectural column-order vocabulary.

objects.name: concrete beam-and-slab floor system
objects.definition: A suspended concrete floor in which a slab spans to downstand, band or other concrete beams that carry loads onward to columns or walls.
functions: Divide floor action between slab and beams
Span between columns or walls
Provide an explicit beam-supported floor topology

cad.pattern: Slab panels repeated between beam lines
cad.placement: Over column or wall support grid
cad.opening: Openings coordinate with beam and slab reinforcement

notes: Slab and beams may be poured monolithically but remain separate role objects for drawing, reinforcement and quantities.

objects.name: one-way ribbed concrete slab
objects.definition: A suspended floor with a relatively thin topping flange cast integrally over closely spaced parallel concrete ribs spanning mainly in one direction.
functions: Reduce concrete away from the rib-and-flange load path
Span mainly in one direction
Support the structural topping flange

cad.pattern: Parallel repeated ribs beneath a continuous topping flange
cad.placement: Between beams, walls or other support lines
cad.opening: Openings interrupt ribs only with designed trimming

notes: The word joist can mean the concrete rib or the whole floor family; keep the rib as its own member.

objects.name: concrete slab rib
objects.definition: A narrow repeated concrete beam formed integrally beneath a ribbed or waffle slab topping flange.
functions: Carry slab actions along its span
Stiffen the topping flange
Transfer loads to beams, walls or columns

cad.pattern: Regular parallel linear members
cad.placement: Below and integral with the topping flange
cad.opening: Cannot be removed for a service opening without designed trimming

notes: Reuse the existing foundation waffle rib for ground-supported raft construction; this object is for suspended systems.

objects.name: suspended waffle concrete slab
objects.definition: A suspended floor with a topping flange over intersecting ribs arranged in two directions to form a repeated coffering pattern on the soffit.
functions: Carry two-way floor actions through intersecting ribs
Reduce concrete between rib zones
Create a stiff cellular slab system
materials: removable or permanent coffers where selected

cad.pattern: Orthogonal repeated rib grid with recessed soffit coffers
cad.placement: Between or over column, beam or wall supports
cad.opening: Coordinate penetrations with ribs and solid support zones

notes: The name describes a suspended cellular slab here; always resolve against waffle raft before generating geometry.

objects.name: suspended waffle slab coffer
objects.definition: A repeated recessed soffit cell bounded by intersecting concrete ribs in a suspended waffle slab.
functions: Represent concrete omitted between ribs
Define the soffit cell pattern
Coordinate formwork or permanent coffer geometry

cad.pattern: Repeated cell grid between slab ribs
cad.placement: In the soffit between intersecting ribs
cad.opening: The coffer is itself omitted concrete; services require separate openings
cad.load: No load-bearing material unless a retained product has a documented role

notes: A removable mould creates the recess but does not remain in the building; a permanent coffer is a separate retained object.

objects.name: composite steel-deck concrete slab
objects.definition: A concrete slab cast on profiled steel decking where the concrete, deck and supporting steel system have the documented composite or permanent-formwork roles.
functions: Form a suspended floor
Use profiled deck as construction support and retained component
Transfer composite actions where designed
not_synonyms: steel deck used only as formwork automatically

ncc_references.relationship: Includes the AS/NZS 2327 composite steel-concrete construction route among structural design references.

cad.pattern: Profiled deck sheets spanning to steel supports with concrete above
cad.placement: Over structural steel beams or walls
cad.opening: Deck and concrete openings require coordinated trimming
cad.load: Composite only where designed and connected accordingly

notes: Retained steel deck geometry does not prove composite action; deck-only formwork and composite deck are different evidence states.

objects.name: structural concrete topping
objects.definition: A cast concrete layer placed over precast units, deck or an existing structural substrate and designed to contribute to the completed structural floor action.
functions: Connect or distribute actions across supporting units
Provide composite structural depth where designed
Form the upper structural surface

cad.pattern: Continuous or jointed cast layer across supporting units
cad.placement: On precast panels, hollowcore units, double tees or deck
cad.opening: Continue only around coordinated penetrations and shafts
cad.load: Structural only when documented as composite or load distributing

notes: Calling any screed a topping must not grant it a structural role.

objects.name: structural concrete beam
objects.definition: A horizontal or sloping concrete member that spans between supports and transfers loads from slabs, walls or other members.
functions: Span between supports
Carry flexure, shear and other designed actions
Support slabs, walls or secondary members

cad.pattern: Linear member between supports
cad.placement: Below, within or above supported slab or wall geometry
cad.start: Support face, centreline or documented joint
cad.opening: Web openings require explicit structural design

notes: Beam role is structural, while downstand, band and transfer describe physical profile or function refinements.

objects.name: downstand concrete beam
objects.definition: A concrete beam whose body projects below the adjacent slab soffit along its span.
functions: Support a slab or other members
Provide structural depth below the slab
Transfer actions to columns, walls or other beams

cad.pattern: Linear projection below slab soffit
cad.placement: Integral with or supporting a slab
cad.opening: Penetrations require designed web-opening geometry

notes: The profile affects ceilings and services and therefore remains distinct from a hidden band beam.

objects.name: concrete band beam
objects.definition: A broad relatively shallow concrete beam formed within or close to the slab depth to create a wide support band with limited soffit projection.
functions: Collect slab actions over a broad strip
Transfer loads between columns or walls
Limit local downstand depth where designed

cad.pattern: Wide linear support strip through slab field
cad.placement: Within or slightly below the slab depth between supports
cad.opening: Coordinate services with dense beam reinforcement or tendons

notes: A dimensionally wide region is not automatically a band beam unless it has the documented beam role.

objects.name: concrete transfer beam
objects.definition: A concrete beam designed to collect loads from columns, walls or framing above and redirect them to a different support arrangement below.
functions: Transfer discontinuous vertical load paths
Support offset columns, walls or major framing
Distribute concentrated actions to receiving supports
not_synonyms: ordinary beam solely because it is deep

cad.pattern: Major linear member below offset supported elements
cad.placement: At a change in structural grid or load path
cad.opening: Openings are exceptional and require explicit design

notes: Transfer is a load-path role that must come from engineering evidence, not member depth alone.

objects.name: structural concrete column
objects.definition: A predominantly vertical concrete member transferring concentrated floor, roof or frame actions between levels and into supports below.
functions: Carry axial and bending actions
Support beams, slabs or walls
Continue vertical load paths through the structure

cad.pattern: Repeated at structural grid points
cad.placement: Between foundation, floor and roof levels
cad.start: Footing, transfer member or lower joint
cad.end: Upper joint, slab or beam interface
cad.opening: No uncoordinated service penetrations

notes: Store storey-by-storey segments and joints explicitly so bar laps, precast connections and pour breaks can differ.

objects.name: structural concrete wall
objects.definition: A vertical or sloping concrete plate member carrying gravity, lateral, retaining or enclosure actions according to its documented structural role.
functions: Carry in-plane or out-of-plane actions
Support floors, roofs or earth where designed
Form a durable wall plane

cad.pattern: Continuous or jointed vertical plate
cad.placement: Along structural wall lines
cad.opening: Door, window and service openings require explicit boundary reinforcement

notes: Wall, shear wall, core wall, retaining wall and precast wall can share shape while having different roles and connections.

objects.name: concrete shear wall
objects.definition: A structural concrete wall assigned to resist lateral actions through in-plane shear, bending and axial behaviour within the building stability system.
functions: Resist lateral actions
Transfer overturning and shear to foundations
Stabilise floors and frames

cad.pattern: Continuous wall lines connected to floor diaphragms
cad.placement: At documented stability-system locations
cad.opening: Openings create designed piers and coupling regions

notes: Shear-wall status is a design assignment and must not be inferred from thickness or position.

objects.name: concrete core wall system
objects.definition: A connected group of concrete walls enclosing lift, stair or service spaces and often contributing to the building's gravity and lateral load paths.
functions: Enclose a vertical core
Provide structural continuity around shafts
Resist gravity and lateral actions where designed

cad.pattern: Closed or partly closed vertical wall group
cad.placement: Around stairs, lifts or service shafts
cad.opening: Doorways, landings and service penetrations remain explicit
cad.load: Core stability and gravity roles only as designed

notes: The enclosed void and the concrete walls are separate geometry; do not fill the shaft as solid concrete.

objects.name: concrete pedestal
objects.definition: A short squat concrete support projecting above a footing, slab or member to receive a column, bearing, machine or other concentrated component.
functions: Raise and support a concentrated load
Spread actions into the supporting concrete
Provide anchorage and bearing geometry

cad.pattern: Discrete supports at selected load points
cad.placement: On a footing, pile cap, slab or beam
cad.opening: Contains coordinated anchor pockets or sleeves only

notes: Plinth can also mean a non-structural raised base; preserve the documented support role.

objects.name: concrete corbel
objects.definition: A short concrete projection from a column or wall that provides a bearing seat for a beam, slab or other supported element.
functions: Create a local bearing ledge
Transfer concentrated bearing actions into its host
Locate a supported member
materials: bearing pad or plate where selected

cad.pattern: Discrete projection at support locations
cad.placement: From a concrete column or wall face
cad.opening: No uncoordinated penetrations through the corbel zone

notes: A corbel supports through a designed short projection; a decorative moulding with the same silhouette is not the same object.

objects.name: structural concrete upstand
objects.definition: A continuous or local concrete projection rising above a slab or beam surface to form a structural edge, kerb, wall base or support feature.
functions: Raise a concrete edge or support line
Stiffen or contain the slab edge where designed
Provide a base for barriers, walls or waterproofing interfaces

cad.pattern: Continuous or segmented raised run
cad.placement: On or integral with a slab or beam edge
cad.opening: Breaks at documented drainage or access openings
cad.load: Structural only where assigned by design

notes: Upstand describes geometry; kerb, hob, parapet and beam describe possible roles that must remain explicit.

objects.name: concrete wall or column kicker
objects.definition: A short first lift or nib of concrete cast at the base of a later wall or column to locate formwork and establish the base geometry.
functions: Locate later wall or column forms
Establish the base line and thickness
Form part of the permanent concrete joint detail

cad.pattern: Short base projection following the later wall or column line
cad.placement: On a slab or footing below a later vertical pour
cad.opening: Coordinates doorway and service crossings
cad.load: Permanent base geometry; structural role follows design

notes: The permanent concrete kicker and a temporary diagonal brace sometimes called a kicker are not synonyms.

objects.name: concrete deep-foundation system
objects.definition: A foundation assembly using piles and caps or ground beams to transfer building actions to deeper soil or rock than ordinary shallow footings.
functions: Transfer actions to deep founding strata
Connect piles into the building load path
Coordinate pile layout, caps, ground beams and column or wall supports
materials: steel casing or sections where selected

ncc_references.relationship: Provides the structural Deemed-to-Satisfy route to AS 2159 for piling.

cad.pattern: Pile points or rows connected by caps and ground beams
cad.placement: Below the supported building at geotechnically designed locations
cad.end: Cap, ground beam or supported superstructure
cad.opening: Services and excavations coordinate with pile exclusion zones

notes: Pile depth, diameter, capacity and founding level require geotechnical and structural evidence and must never be guessed from the building above.

objects.name: concrete pile group
objects.definition: Two or more piles arranged and connected to act beneath one cap, wall, column or other supported foundation zone.
functions: Combine resistance from multiple piles
Support a pile cap or ground beam
Distribute concentrated actions across the pile layout

cad.pattern: Repeated pile axes below one cap or support zone
cad.placement: Under a cap, ground beam, wall or column
cad.opening: Keep excavations and services outside designed pile and cap zones

notes: Geometric proximity alone does not prove piles were designed as one group.

objects.name: structural concrete pile
objects.definition: A slender deep-foundation element containing concrete and extending into the ground to transfer building actions through shaft resistance, toe resistance or both.
functions: Transfer actions to deeper soil or rock
Connect the supported cap to the founding zone
Provide a durable embedded foundation element

cad.pattern: Single deep linear foundation element
cad.placement: Below cap or ground beam into soil or rock
cad.end: Cut-off head within cap or beam
cad.opening: No service penetrations unless specifically designed

notes: Pier is too ambiguous to accept as an exact synonym because Australian usage can also mean a shallow bulk pier or masonry support.

objects.name: bored cast-in-place concrete pile
objects.definition: A concrete pile formed by drilling or excavating a shaft in the ground, placing reinforcement where required and filling the excavation with concrete.
functions: Create a deep foundation without driving a finished pile
Transfer actions through the completed shaft and toe
Receive a pile cap or ground beam at cut-off level
materials: temporary or permanent casing where selected

cad.pattern: Vertical or raking shafts at designed setout points
cad.placement: Formed in excavated ground below the supported structure
cad.opening: The construction bore is replaced by concrete in the completed state

notes: The empty bore and temporary support fluid are construction states, not completed pile geometry.

objects.name: continuous-flight-auger concrete pile
objects.definition: A cast-in-place pile formed using a continuous-flight auger, with concrete or grout placed as the auger is withdrawn and reinforcement inserted into the fresh material.
functions: Form a deep pile with continuous-auger installation
Transfer actions through shaft and toe resistance
Connect to a cap or ground beam

cad.pattern: Repeated deep shafts at designed setout
cad.placement: Installed through soil below cap or ground beam
cad.opening: No retained auger void

notes: CFA identifies an installation topology, not merely a cylindrical shape.

objects.name: driven precast concrete pile
objects.definition: A factory or casting-yard concrete pile installed into the ground by driving, pressing or another documented displacement method before connection to the foundation above.
functions: Displace or penetrate ground during installation
Transfer foundation actions through a prefabricated pile
Provide a controlled manufactured pile section
materials: pile shoe or splice where selected

cad.pattern: Repeated manufactured linear units driven from ground level
cad.placement: Below pile caps or ground beams
cad.opening: Splice joints remain explicit where multiple lengths are joined

notes: Manufacture, transport, driving and final embedded states require different support and damage records.

objects.name: driven cast-in-place concrete pile
objects.definition: A pile formed by driving a casing, tube or displacement former and then casting concrete in the created shaft, with the casing retained or withdrawn as documented.
functions: Create a displacement pile
Form the permanent pile concrete in the ground
Transfer actions to deeper strata

cad.pattern: Repeated displacement-formed shafts
cad.placement: Below cap or beam in installed ground
cad.opening: Temporary former geometry is removed unless casing is documented as permanent

notes: Retained casing must be drawn separately from temporary casing.

objects.name: grouted micropile
objects.definition: A small-diameter drilled and grouted deep-foundation element containing a central steel bar, bars or section and transferring actions through the grout-ground interface.
functions: Provide deep support in restricted or retrofit conditions
Transfer axial and sometimes lateral actions
Connect a steel core to the supported foundation through grout

cad.pattern: Small-diameter linear elements at designed setout
cad.placement: Drilled through soil, rock or existing foundations
cad.start: Bonded toe or lower bond zone
cad.opening: Drill hole becomes grout body around the steel core

notes: Micropile, soil nail and ground anchor can look similar but have different load paths and acceptance evidence.

objects.name: permanent pile casing
objects.definition: A steel or other approved tubular casing deliberately left around part or all of a cast-in-place pile after installation.
functions: Retain ground or isolate the shaft during construction
Remain as permanent pile boundary where documented
Contribute to durability or structural action only where designed

cad.pattern: Concentric tube around pile shaft
cad.placement: Around selected length of cast-in-place pile
cad.opening: Filled with pile concrete around internal reinforcement
cad.load: Structural only where included in design

notes: Temporary casing must be excluded from final geometry once withdrawn.

objects.name: pile reinforcement cage
objects.definition: A prefabricated cylindrical or shaped assembly of longitudinal reinforcing bars and ties installed inside a cast-in-place concrete pile.
functions: Reinforce the pile shaft
Maintain longitudinal bars in their designed arrangement
Connect pile reinforcement into the cap or ground beam

cad.pattern: Longitudinal bars held by repeated circular ties or spiral
cad.placement: Within cast-in-place pile concrete
cad.end: Pile head projection or cage top
cad.opening: Maintain placement access and concrete flow paths

notes: The cage can be shorter than the pile; model its actual extent rather than filling every pile automatically.

objects.name: concrete pile cap
objects.definition: A reinforced concrete block or thick plate connecting one or more pile heads to a column, wall, pedestal or ground beam above.
functions: Collect actions from the supported element
Distribute actions into pile heads
Tie the pile group into the foundation system

cad.pattern: Discrete thick foundation block around one or more pile heads
cad.placement: At pile cut-off level below a column, wall or pedestal
cad.opening: Coordinate services outside pile-head and strut-and-tie zones

notes: A cap over one pile is still distinct from the pile itself and may provide anchorage, bearing and load-spreading geometry.

objects.name: concrete pile ground beam
objects.definition: A reinforced concrete beam at or below ground level spanning between pile caps or piles and supporting walls, columns or floor edges.
functions: Connect deep-foundation supports
Carry walls or concentrated loads between piles
Tie the foundation system where designed

cad.pattern: Linear network between pile supports
cad.placement: At or below ground beneath walls or columns
cad.opening: Services require coordinated sleeves or local design
cad.load: Foundation beam spanning between deep supports

notes: Whether the beam bears on soil or spans clear is a design input with major consequences and must remain explicit.

objects.name: placed concrete reinforcement assembly
objects.definition: The complete arrangement of reinforcing bars, mesh, fitments, splices, ties, chairs and spacers fixed in position before concrete surrounds them.
functions: Hold every reinforcement item in its designed topology
Maintain cover and spacing during concrete placement
Provide the embedded reinforcement system in the hardened element

cad.pattern: Layered bars, mesh and fitments tied into a stable three-dimensional arrangement
cad.placement: Inside the concrete volume before placement
cad.start: First designed bar layer or cage end
cad.opening: Bars are trimmed, diverted or added only from documented detailing

notes: The existing foundations reinforcement assembly remains the ground-slab parent; this object covers wider structural concrete placement and cage topology.

objects.name: reinforcement cage
objects.definition: A three-dimensional prefixed arrangement of longitudinal bars and transverse fitments shaped to reinforce a beam, column, wall boundary, pile or other concrete member.
functions: Keep longitudinal and transverse reinforcement together
Match the host member's reinforcement topology
Allow the complete set to be placed and inspected as an assembly

cad.pattern: Longitudinal bars enclosed or crossed by repeated fitments
cad.placement: Within the host member envelope
cad.opening: Cage geometry coordinates with penetrations and cast-ins

notes: Cage is an assembly; each bar and fitment remains selectable and schedulable.

objects.name: reinforcement bar mat
objects.definition: A generally planar field of intersecting reinforcing bars fixed together as one reinforcement layer in a slab, wall, cap or foundation element.
functions: Create a two-direction reinforcement layer
Maintain bar spacing and order
Reinforce a plate or wall field
not_synonyms: one bar layer without crossings automatically

cad.pattern: Two crossing bar fields on a common layer
cad.placement: At top, bottom or face layer of a slab, wall or cap
cad.opening: Trim and supplement around documented openings

notes: A tied bar mat and a factory welded mesh sheet may perform similar roles but have different bar identity, laps and scheduling.

objects.name: deformed reinforcing bar
objects.definition: A solid steel reinforcing bar with a patterned surface intended to develop bond with the surrounding concrete.
functions: Reinforce concrete in tension, compression or shear as designed
Develop bond along its embedded length
Form straight or scheduled bent bar shapes

cad.pattern: Scheduled linear or bent bar path
cad.placement: Within concrete cover and spacing envelope
cad.start: Development, anchorage, splice or free end
cad.end: Opposite development, anchorage, splice or end
cad.opening: May divert only according to documented detailing

notes: A rendered rib pattern is visual only; actual product designation and traceability are evidence attributes.

objects.name: plain round reinforcing bar
objects.definition: A smooth round steel bar used as concrete reinforcement or as a dowel, fitment or other documented reinforcing component.
functions: Provide a selected smooth reinforcing or dowel element
Allow slip where a sleeved joint design requires it
Form scheduled fitments or connections

cad.pattern: Straight or scheduled shaped bar
cad.placement: Within concrete or across a documented joint
cad.opening: Coordinates with joints and cast-ins
cad.load: Reinforcement or dowel role only as detailed

notes: Smooth surface does not by itself identify a dowel; role and joint treatment are separate attributes.

objects.name: longitudinal reinforcing bar
objects.definition: A reinforcing bar running mainly along the length or height of a beam, column, wall boundary, pile or similar member.
functions: Provide the member's longitudinal reinforcement
Carry axial or flexural actions as designed
Connect through laps, couplers or anchorages
not_synonyms: main bar automatically in every context

cad.pattern: Repeated bars parallel to the host member axis
cad.placement: Within a beam, column, wall boundary or pile cage
cad.opening: Bar path coordinates around openings only by design

notes: Longitudinal is a role and direction; the physical product may be a deformed bar, headed bar or coupled length.

objects.name: transverse reinforcing bar
objects.definition: A reinforcing bar running across the primary member or slab direction to distribute actions, restrain longitudinal bars or provide shear and confinement roles.
functions: Cross or restrain primary reinforcement
Distribute loads or cracking effects
Provide transverse shear or confinement reinforcement where detailed

cad.pattern: Repeated bars across the primary axis or reinforcement direction
cad.placement: Within a slab mat, wall face or member cage
cad.opening: Trim and supplement around openings as detailed

notes: Distribution, temperature, shrinkage, shear and confinement are related roles but not automatic synonyms.

objects.name: starter reinforcing bar
objects.definition: A reinforcing bar projecting from an earlier concrete pour or connection system to lap, couple or develop into a later wall, column, slab or other element.
functions: Connect reinforcement across staged construction
Locate and develop the later element
Transfer designed actions through the joint

cad.pattern: Repeated projecting bars along a construction interface
cad.placement: Across an earlier-to-later concrete pour joint
cad.start: Development inside earlier concrete or coupler
cad.end: Development or lap inside later concrete
cad.opening: Coordinate bars around openings and waterstops

notes: Starter describes staged connection; dowel can instead describe shear transfer or alignment across a movement joint.

objects.name: concrete joint dowel bar
objects.definition: A bar crossing a concrete joint to transfer shear or maintain alignment while allowing or restraining longitudinal movement according to the joint design.
functions: Transfer load across a joint
Maintain adjacent slab or wall alignment
Permit selected movement when sleeved or debonded

cad.pattern: Repeated straight bars perpendicular to a joint
cad.placement: Centred or otherwise detailed across a concrete joint
cad.end: Embedment or movement sleeve in second side
cad.opening: Joint gap and sleeve geometry remain explicit

notes: The model must preserve which end is bonded, sleeved or capped; a solid bar through both sides can accidentally restrain a movement joint.

objects.name: L-shaped reinforcing bar
objects.definition: A scheduled reinforcing bar with one principal bend creating two legs used at corners, ends, junctions or anchorage zones.
functions: Turn reinforcement around a corner or junction
Develop one leg into each connected zone
Provide a scheduled bent-bar connection

cad.pattern: Discrete or repeated bent bars
cad.placement: At concrete corners, junctions and ends
cad.opening: Coordinates with cover and neighbouring bars

notes: Bend dimensions and orientation come from the bar schedule, not a generic 90-degree default.

objects.name: U-shaped reinforcing bar
objects.definition: A scheduled reinforcing bar with two generally parallel legs joined by a bent base, used to wrap, anchor or connect reinforcement zones.
functions: Wrap an edge or member zone
Develop two legs into concrete
Connect or confine selected reinforcement regions

cad.pattern: Discrete or repeated U-shaped paths
cad.placement: At edges, anchorage zones or around other reinforcement
cad.opening: Inside clearance and cover remain explicit

notes: Hairpin is accepted only as related because it can describe particular anchorage or anti-burst details rather than every U bar.

objects.name: hooked reinforcing bar
objects.definition: A reinforcing bar with a scheduled bent hook at one or both ends to provide anchorage or fit within a confined concrete zone.
functions: Anchor a bar end
Fit development into a limited zone
Engage surrounding concrete and transverse reinforcement as detailed

cad.pattern: Linear bar with one or two scheduled end hooks
cad.placement: Within a confined anchorage or member end zone
cad.opening: Hook orientation coordinates with cover and congestion

notes: Hook geometry must be schedule-driven; do not make all short bars hooked by default.

objects.name: closed reinforcing stirrup
objects.definition: A closed or properly closed-loop reinforcing fitment surrounding longitudinal bars in a beam, column or similar member.
functions: Provide transverse shear or torsion reinforcement where designed
Confine concrete and longitudinal bars
Hold the cage cross-section

cad.pattern: Repeated closed loops along the member axis
cad.placement: Around longitudinal cage bars
cad.opening: Loop encloses the detailed cage envelope

notes: Stirrup, tie, fitment and ligature overlap in trade usage; preserve actual shape and function.

objects.name: open reinforcing stirrup
objects.definition: A U-shaped or otherwise open reinforcing fitment placed around selected longitudinal bars without forming one closed loop by itself.
functions: Provide transverse reinforcement in the documented arrangement
Support or restrain selected cage bars
Combine with capping bars or other fitments where detailed

cad.pattern: Repeated open fitments along cage axis
cad.placement: Around or beneath selected longitudinal bars
cad.opening: Open side and companion bar relationship remain explicit

notes: Do not close an open stirrup automatically; its capping or companion reinforcement is separate geometry.

objects.name: spiral reinforcement
objects.definition: A continuous reinforcing bar or wire wound helically around longitudinal reinforcement in a circular or other compatible concrete member.
functions: Confine the concrete core
Restrain longitudinal bars
Provide continuous transverse reinforcement along the member

cad.pattern: Continuous helical path
cad.placement: Around longitudinal bars in a pile, column or anchorage zone
cad.opening: Pitch and cage clearances remain explicit

notes: A series of individual circular ties can look similar in coarse geometry but has separate laps and spacing.

objects.name: headed reinforcing bar
objects.definition: A reinforcing bar with a mechanically attached or integrally formed head that develops bar force through bearing in the surrounding concrete.
functions: Provide compact bar-end anchorage
Transfer bar force through the head and surrounding concrete
Reduce reliance on a long hook or straight development where designed

cad.pattern: Bar path terminating in a discrete enlarged head
cad.placement: At a congested anchorage or member end zone
cad.opening: Head clearance and cover remain explicit

notes: The head is part of the reinforcement product; it is not interchangeable with an anchor plate unless the system is documented that way.

objects.name: reinforcing bar bundle
objects.definition: Two or more reinforcing bars intentionally grouped in contact or close arrangement and treated as a documented reinforcement bundle.
functions: Concentrate longitudinal reinforcement
Fit required steel area into a selected zone
Maintain the detailed grouped-bar topology

cad.pattern: Parallel grouped bar paths
cad.placement: Within a congested cage or member zone
cad.opening: Individual bars remain explicit within the bundle

notes: A visual cluster is not enough; bundle status changes detailing and must be documented.

objects.name: reinforcing bar lap splice assembly
objects.definition: A connection zone where two reinforcing bars overlap for a documented length so force can transfer through bond and surrounding concrete.
functions: Continue reinforcement across separate bar lengths
Transfer force through overlapping embedment
Locate a staged or scheduled splice zone

cad.pattern: Two bar paths overlapping within one splice zone
cad.placement: At documented low-risk or staged reinforcement locations
cad.opening: Maintain cover, spacing and concrete flow around both bars

notes: Do not calculate or default lap length from diameter alone; concrete, bar, stress, confinement and authorised design rules matter.

objects.name: mechanical reinforcing bar splice assembly
objects.definition: A connection between reinforcing bars using a purpose-designed mechanical coupler or sleeve rather than relying on an overlapping bonded length.
functions: Continue bar force through a mechanical connector
Reduce or avoid lap congestion
Connect staged or prefabricated reinforcement

cad.pattern: Discrete connectors on aligned or documented offset bar ends
cad.placement: At scheduled bar continuation locations
cad.opening: Connector envelope and installation access remain clear
cad.load: Mechanical reinforcement continuity only with qualified system

notes: A cylindrical shape on a bar is not proof of a qualified coupler; product, installation and inspection evidence are essential.

objects.name: reinforcing bar coupler
objects.definition: A discrete mechanical connector that grips, threads onto or otherwise engages two prepared reinforcing bar ends to form a mechanical splice.
functions: Join two reinforcing bars
Transfer bar force through the mechanical connection
Provide a compact continuation detail

cad.pattern: Discrete sleeves at bar joints
cad.placement: Concentric or system-defined around connected bar ends
cad.opening: Maintain clearance for installation and concrete flow

notes: Threaded, swaged and bolted systems can share a cylinder envelope but need different attributes and installation evidence.

objects.name: grouted reinforcing bar sleeve
objects.definition: A hollow sleeve receiving one or more reinforcing bar ends and filled with a compatible structural grout to form a qualified bar connection.
functions: Connect reinforcement across precast or staged joints
Transfer bar force through grout and sleeve
Accommodate controlled erection tolerance

cad.pattern: Discrete sleeves aligned with projecting bars
cad.placement: Within precast element ends or staged concrete joints
cad.opening: Model grout ports and joint access where they remain relevant

notes: An unfilled sleeve is an incomplete connection state; the model must distinguish empty, grouted and verified states.

objects.name: reinforcement cover spacer
objects.definition: A small component fixed to or placed against reinforcement to maintain its designed side, soffit or face distance from formwork or ground.
functions: Maintain concrete cover
Prevent reinforcement contacting formwork or substrate
Hold cage position during concrete placement
materials: fibre cement or approved spacer material
not_synonyms: bar chair carrying vertical layers automatically

cad.pattern: Repeated discrete contacts between cage and form face
cad.placement: On side or soffit reinforcement facing the concrete boundary
cad.opening: Do not obstruct concrete flow or expose incompatible material

notes: Cover is a dimension; the spacer is the physical component used to maintain it.

objects.name: plastic bar chair
objects.definition: A moulded plastic chair supporting reinforcing bars or mesh above formwork, membrane or a substrate at a selected height.
functions: Support reinforcement at elevation
Maintain concrete cover during placement
Resist construction handling within its selected rating

cad.pattern: Repeated discrete supports below bars or mesh
cad.placement: On formwork, membrane or chair bases
cad.opening: Maintain concrete flow around and within the chair
cad.load: Temporary construction support retained in concrete

notes: Select height, strength grade and exposure suitability from project requirements; one default chair is unsafe and inaccurate.

objects.name: plastic-tipped wire bar chair
objects.definition: A bent steel-wire reinforcement chair whose feet are capped with plastic to separate exposed steel ends from the formed concrete surface.
functions: Support reinforcement at elevation
Maintain cover over formwork
Provide a high-open-area chair geometry

cad.pattern: Repeated wire frames under reinforcement
cad.placement: On slab or beam formwork
cad.opening: Keep plastic tips intact and concrete access open
cad.load: Temporary construction support retained in concrete

notes: Exposure limitations differ from plastic or concrete chairs and must be selected from current project evidence.

objects.name: concrete bar chair
objects.definition: A small purpose-made concrete support carrying reinforcement at the selected cover or layer height and becoming bonded into the placed concrete.
functions: Support reinforcement
Maintain cover and layer separation
Provide a cementitious support suitable for selected exposure conditions

cad.pattern: Repeated discrete cementitious supports
cad.placement: Below heavy reinforcement or in selected exposure conditions
cad.opening: Concrete placement must fully surround the chair
cad.load: Temporary construction support retained and bonded in concrete

notes: A loose offcut or broken block is not accepted automatically as a compliant purpose-made chair.

objects.name: continuous bar chair
objects.definition: An elongated reinforcement support with repeated legs or a continuous profile carrying bars or mesh along a line rather than at isolated points.
functions: Support a reinforcement layer continuously or at close repeated legs
Maintain a selected elevation
Speed support setout over slab or precast beds

cad.pattern: Parallel support runs beneath reinforcement
cad.placement: On formwork or lower reinforcement layer
cad.opening: Break around penetrations and preserve concrete flow

notes: Continuous means the product can carry along a run; it does not mean reinforcement may bear on an arbitrary loose bar.

objects.name: reinforcement support hurdle
objects.definition: A fabricated steel support frame or trestle used to hold an upper reinforcement mat or heavy bars above a lower layer at the required separation.
functions: Support heavy top reinforcement
Maintain layer separation
Transfer construction loads to lower support points during placing

cad.pattern: Repeated transverse support frames below top reinforcement
cad.placement: Between lower support layer and upper bars or mat
cad.opening: Coordinate legs with lower bars and concrete access
cad.load: Temporary construction support retained in concrete

notes: A hurdle may be fabricated from reinforcement but does not automatically count toward structural reinforcement unless the design says so.

objects.name: structural concrete joint system
objects.definition: The complete physical interface between separate concrete placements or movement zones, including the gap or contact faces, keys, dowels, reinforcement treatment, waterstops, fillers and seals selected for its role.
functions: Divide concrete into designed pours or movement units
Transfer, release or isolate actions as documented
Coordinate water, air and finish continuity across the interface
not_synonyms: ordinary pour line with unknown role

cad.pattern: Continuous interface through the concrete element or selected depth
cad.placement: At documented pour, shrinkage, isolation or building movement lines
cad.opening: The joint gap, groove or face is explicit rather than represented only by a line
cad.load: Transfer and movement role only as designed

notes: Construction, contraction, isolation and expansion describe different intent; never choose one solely from a visible line.

objects.name: concrete construction joint
objects.definition: A planned interface where one concrete placement stops and a later placement continues against or connects to the earlier hardened concrete.
functions: Define a practical pour boundary
Connect staged concrete work
Transfer or release actions according to its key, reinforcement and surface treatment

cad.pattern: Continuous staged-pour interface
cad.placement: At designed stopping points in slabs, beams, walls or columns
cad.opening: Joint face, key and waterstop geometry remain explicit
cad.load: Continuity or slip follows documented detail

notes: A cold joint describes an undesirable or separately assessed placement condition, not an automatic synonym for every planned construction joint.

objects.name: concrete contraction joint
objects.definition: A deliberately weakened or formed joint intended to localise shortening and cracking from concrete shrinkage or temperature contraction.
functions: Create a preferred crack-control plane
Allow selected contraction
Coordinate load transfer and surface sealing where required

cad.pattern: Repeated control lines through selected slab or wall depth
cad.placement: At documented shrinkage-control locations
cad.opening: Surface groove and deeper induced plane are separate attributes
cad.load: Load transfer follows dowel or aggregate-interlock design

notes: Control joint is common Australian usage but can also mean lining or masonry movement joints; the concrete qualifier is essential.

objects.name: concrete isolation joint
objects.definition: A full-depth separation around a column, wall, footing, machine base or adjacent slab intended to reduce transfer of movement or restraint between the concrete parts.
functions: Separate adjoining concrete elements
Allow differential movement
Prevent unwanted restraint or load transfer except through selected components

cad.pattern: Closed perimeter or continuous separating line
cad.placement: Around columns, walls, bases or between independently moving slabs
cad.opening: Gap remains through the intended depth
cad.load: Isolation unless selected dowels provide transfer

notes: An isolation joint is not merely an expansion joint with another name; its key intent is separation from an adjoining restraint.

objects.name: concrete expansion joint
objects.definition: A designed gap separating concrete structural units so they can close, open or move relative to each other within a documented movement range.
functions: Accommodate building or element movement
Maintain trafficable, weather, fire or water interfaces where required
Separate structural units without unintended bridging
materials: dowel sleeves or proprietary cover where selected

cad.pattern: Continuous full-depth separation between structural units
cad.placement: At documented building movement lines
cad.opening: Gap must continue through finishes and attachments unless detailed movement components bridge it
cad.load: Separates structural units; selected devices carry only documented actions

notes: Finish layers must follow the structural joint rather than concealing it with rigid material.

objects.name: keyed concrete joint
objects.definition: A concrete joint whose mating faces include a formed tongue, groove or shear key intended to interlock the adjacent placements.
functions: Provide geometric interlock
Transfer selected shear across the joint
Locate adjoining concrete placements

cad.pattern: Continuous or segmented interlocking profile along joint face
cad.placement: Within a construction or selected movement joint
cad.opening: Maintain clearance around waterstop and reinforcement

notes: The key profile may assist shear transfer but does not by itself establish capacity or watertightness.

objects.name: dowelled concrete joint
objects.definition: A concrete joint crossed by a repeated set of aligned dowel bars that transfer selected actions while permitting or restraining movement according to their sleeves and bond treatment.
functions: Transfer load across the joint
Maintain alignment
Allow selected axial movement when detailed

cad.pattern: Repeated bars crossing the joint perpendicular to its route
cad.placement: At slab, wall or precast joint line
cad.opening: Sleeve and gap geometry remain explicit around each dowel

notes: A dowel model must identify its free-moving direction so a joint is not accidentally locked.

objects.name: concrete saw-cut joint groove
objects.definition: A narrow cut made into the hardened or hardening concrete surface to create the top groove and weakened plane of a selected contraction joint.
functions: Create a localised weakened line
Provide a surface recess for sealant where detailed
Make the intended crack-control route explicit

cad.pattern: Narrow continuous surface groove
cad.placement: In the top or exposed face of a concrete element
cad.opening: The groove removes material to the documented depth

notes: Sawing is the operation; this object is the physical groove left behind.

objects.name: compressible concrete joint filler
objects.definition: A compressible strip or board placed through a concrete joint depth to maintain separation and accommodate selected closing movement.
functions: Keep adjacent concrete faces separated
Provide compressible joint backing
Support the intended movement gap below the surface seal
materials: rubberised or bituminous filler where selected

cad.pattern: Continuous strip within joint gap
cad.placement: Between separated concrete faces below the surface seal
cad.opening: Leaves the documented sealant reservoir at the exposed face

notes: Filler and sealant have different depths and functions and must not be collapsed into one material field.

objects.name: concrete joint sealant
objects.definition: A flexible sealant bead installed at the exposed mouth of a concrete joint to limit water, air, debris or contaminants while accommodating documented movement.
functions: Seal the exposed joint mouth
Accommodate selected movement
Protect filler, backing and internal joint components

cad.pattern: Continuous flexible bead at exposed joint face
cad.placement: Over backing rod or bond breaker between prepared concrete edges
cad.opening: Maintains concave, recessed or flush profile as documented

notes: Sealant does not convert a wrongly detailed joint into a movement-capable or watertight structural joint.

objects.name: concrete joint backer rod
objects.definition: A compressible foam rod installed behind concrete joint sealant to control bead depth, provide tooling support and prevent unintended three-sided adhesion.
functions: Control sealant depth
Support the sealant profile
Act as a bond-breaking backing surface

cad.pattern: Continuous cylindrical backing within the joint mouth
cad.placement: Behind sealant and above deeper filler or void
cad.opening: Leaves the selected sealant depth above

notes: A backer rod is reusable vocabulary across facade and concrete joints, but host, movement and compatibility remain joint-specific.

objects.name: structural concrete joint waterstop
objects.definition: A continuous strip or profile embedded in, bonded to or fixed across a concrete joint to obstruct water passage through the joint path.
functions: Create a continuous water barrier through the joint
Bridge the two concrete placements or faces
Coordinate corners, intersections and penetrations

cad.pattern: Continuous barrier centred on or applied across joint route
cad.placement: Within or on the water-facing side of a concrete joint
cad.opening: Factory or site junction pieces maintain continuity

notes: This structural joint waterstop is not the aluminium or polymer angle used at a bathroom threshold.

objects.name: centre-bulb cast-in waterstop
objects.definition: A cast-in waterstop profile with a central bulb or movement zone and embedded flanges extending into the concrete on both sides of a movement joint.
functions: Seal a moving joint
Anchor one side of the profile in each concrete unit
Allow selected joint opening, closing or shear movement

cad.pattern: Continuous profiled strip centred on movement joint
cad.placement: Half embedded in each adjoining concrete placement
cad.opening: Central bulb aligns with the joint gap

notes: The bulb must follow the movement plane; centring the entire profile on concrete rather than the joint defeats its intended topology.

objects.name: hydrophilic concrete joint strip
objects.definition: A compact strip fixed to a prepared first concrete face that swells on sustained water contact to obstruct leakage through a later construction joint.
functions: Seal a construction-joint leakage path
Expand within confinement when exposed to water
Provide a continuous strip around selected intersections and penetrations

cad.pattern: Continuous compact strip on first-pour face
cad.placement: Within the later concrete cover along construction joint
cad.opening: Route continues around penetrations only with documented junctions

notes: Swelling is a product behaviour, not permission to place the strip near an exposed edge without suitable confinement.

objects.name: concrete joint dowel sleeve
objects.definition: A tube or proprietary housing surrounding one end of a joint dowel so that end can slide axially while the dowel continues to transfer selected transverse actions.
functions: Permit axial dowel movement
Maintain dowel alignment
Separate one dowel end from bond to the surrounding concrete

cad.pattern: Repeated sleeves on the selected free ends of joint dowels
cad.placement: Embedded in one side of a dowelled joint
cad.opening: Internal clearance provides the movement path
cad.load: Guide and debonding housing, not a bar splice

notes: Sleeve length and free direction must be explicit; mirroring the detail can change which slab is allowed to move.

objects.name: cast-in concrete embed assembly
objects.definition: A coordinated set of metal, plastic or other components fixed within formwork or reinforcement before the concrete is placed so selected parts remain embedded and available after stripping.
functions: Provide connection, fixing, bearing, service or lifting interfaces
Hold components at the required concrete position
Coordinate reinforcement, cover and formwork openings

cad.pattern: Discrete or linear embedded components at documented setout
cad.placement: Within formwork and reinforcement before concrete placement
cad.end: Exposed face, threaded opening or connected component
cad.opening: Coordinate every embed with reinforcement and concrete edge geometry
cad.load: Structural only where designed and evidenced

notes: Not every cast-in item falls under the same fastening design route; service sleeves, lifting inserts and structural anchor channels retain separate roles.

objects.name: cast-in threaded ferrule
objects.definition: A female-threaded metal insert with an embedded anchorage body cast into concrete to receive a matching bolt or threaded accessory at the surface.
functions: Provide a reusable threaded fixing point
Transfer selected fixing actions into the concrete
Locate attached components at a prepared concrete face

cad.pattern: Discrete inserts on a documented fixing grid
cad.placement: Cast within concrete with thread accessible at the face
cad.opening: Thread void and temporary plug state remain distinct
cad.load: Fixing point only within designed actions

notes: A ferrule for formwork or lifting is not automatically a permanent building fixing; record lifecycle role.

objects.name: cast-in anchor channel
objects.definition: A continuous or segmented steel channel with embedded anchors cast flush with a concrete face to receive movable channel bolts or attached brackets.
functions: Provide an adjustable fixing line
Transfer attached-component actions into concrete
Allow longitudinal bolt positioning within the channel slot

cad.pattern: Linear fixing slot with repeated rear anchors
cad.placement: Flush with or recessed into a concrete face
cad.opening: Slot remains clear after temporary filler removal
cad.load: Adjustable structural or non-structural fixing as designed

notes: A generic slot does not establish anchor capacity; store the selected system and bolt positions.

objects.name: cast-in steel embed plate
objects.definition: A steel plate cast at or near a concrete surface and anchored into the member by studs, bars, lugs or other designed anchorage.
functions: Provide a bearing, bolting or welding face
Transfer attached-member actions into concrete
Create a controlled steel-to-concrete interface

cad.pattern: Discrete plates at connection points
cad.placement: Flush, recessed or embedded at a concrete face
cad.opening: Holes and weld zones remain explicit

notes: The plate, its embedded anchors and later site welds are separate physical parts of one connection assembly.

objects.name: cast-in concrete penetration sleeve
objects.definition: A tubular component fixed through formwork before concrete placement to preserve a circular or shaped passage for a later service, tendon, bolt or other component.
functions: Create and line a concrete penetration
Keep concrete out of the required passage
Coordinate later service installation and sealing

cad.pattern: Discrete tubes through concrete elements
cad.placement: Across the full concrete thickness or selected embedment
cad.opening: The internal bore remains clear and separately sealable

notes: A sleeve coordinates a hole; it does not prove fire, water, acoustic or structural performance of the completed penetration.

objects.name: concrete blockout
objects.definition: A deliberately omitted volume in a concrete placement reserved for later equipment, connection, service, closure pour or access work.
functions: Keep a selected concrete volume empty
Provide later installation or connection access
Define a closure-pour or infill boundary
materials: edge reinforcement and waterstop where selected

cad.pattern: Discrete omitted concrete volume
cad.placement: Within a slab, wall, beam, cap or pedestal
cad.opening: The void is explicit until a separately modelled infill or equipment item occupies it
cad.load: No load-bearing material until completed by design

notes: Temporary foam or timber used to form the void is removed; the resulting opening remains until intentionally filled.

objects.name: formed concrete recess
objects.definition: A local shallow volume omitted from a concrete face to receive a fitting, plate, anchorage, finish, grout cap or other selected component.
functions: Set a component below or behind the main concrete face
Provide clearance for connection work
Create a controlled later patch or cover zone
materials: later grout, patch or component where selected

cad.pattern: Discrete shallow subtraction from concrete face
cad.placement: At anchorages, plates, fittings or finish interfaces
cad.opening: Later patch or component remains a separate object
cad.load: No material within recess until filled

notes: Pocket can also mean a deeper blockout; store depth and intended lifecycle rather than relying on the word alone.

objects.name: cast-in starter-bar box
objects.definition: A recessed box or casing cast into an earlier concrete element containing bent reinforcement that is later exposed and straightened or connected into a subsequent pour.
functions: Store and protect starter bars during the first pour
Create a prepared joint recess
Connect a later slab or wall reinforcement field

cad.pattern: Linear recessed boxes along staged slab or wall joints
cad.placement: At the face of the first concrete pour
cad.opening: The cover is temporary; the recess and released bars connect to the later pour

notes: The temporary cover and foam do not remain in the completed joint.

objects.name: formed concrete shear key
objects.definition: A projecting or recessed concrete profile at a joint or bearing interface intended to interlock adjoining concrete or grout and transfer selected shear.
functions: Provide geometric interlock
Locate an adjoining element or closure pour
Transfer selected shear across the interface
materials: grout at adjoining interface where selected

cad.pattern: Continuous or discrete matching projections and recesses
cad.placement: At concrete joints, precast interfaces or closure strips
cad.opening: The female key is omitted concrete; the male key is retained concrete

notes: Male and female key geometry must be kept complementary; do not model both as added solids.

objects.name: post-tensioning system
objects.definition: The complete set of tendons, ducts or sheaths, anchorages, grout or grease, vents, couplers, supports and anchorage-zone reinforcement used to post-tension a concrete element.
functions: Introduce prestressing force after the concrete hardens
Maintain and protect tendon paths
Transfer tendon force through anchorages and concrete zones

cad.pattern: Curved or straight tendon runs between anchorages
cad.placement: Inside a post-tensioned concrete member
cad.start: Dead end, coupler or first anchorage
cad.opening: Tendon exclusion zones and deviations remain explicit
cad.load: Prestressing system only with engineered design and verified stressing

notes: Geometry can document the selected system but cannot calculate or certify prestress, losses, elongation, grouting or acceptance.

objects.name: bonded multistrand post-tensioning tendon
objects.definition: A post-tensioning tendon containing multiple prestressing strands inside a common duct that is filled with grout after stressing so the strands bond to the surrounding member.
functions: Carry prestressing force through multiple strands
Transfer force at anchorages and through bonded grout
Protect and locate strands within a common duct

cad.pattern: One duct path containing repeated strand paths
cad.placement: Along a designed profile within concrete
cad.opening: Maintain tendon and anchorage exclusion zones

notes: The duct and grout remain distinct physical components even though the grouted tendon acts as one bonded assembly.

objects.name: unbonded monostrand post-tensioning tendon
objects.definition: A single prestressing strand coated with corrosion-protective grease and enclosed in an extruded plastic sheath, anchored at its ends without grout bonding along its length.
functions: Carry post-tensioning force through one strand
Allow strand movement relative to the concrete during stressing
Protect the strand with grease and continuous sheathing

cad.pattern: Individual sheathed strand paths grouped into bands where designed
cad.placement: Along a supported profile within concrete
cad.opening: Preserve no-cut and exclusion zones around tendons

notes: Do not generate a grout-filled duct around an unbonded monostrand; its grease and sheath are the permanent protection system.

objects.name: prestressing steel strand
objects.definition: A high-strength steel strand made from helically arranged wires and used as the tensile element in pre-tensioned or post-tensioned concrete.
functions: Carry high tensile prestressing force
Transfer force through anchorages or bonded length
Follow the selected tendon or casting-bed path

cad.pattern: Continuous high-strength steel path
cad.placement: Inside tendon duct, monostrand sheath or pre-tensioning line
cad.opening: No arbitrary cutting or drilling through recorded path

notes: Strand is the steel product; tendon is the assembly and force path containing one or more strands.

objects.name: post-tensioning tendon duct
objects.definition: A continuous corrugated or otherwise formed enclosure creating the internal passage for one or more bonded post-tensioning strands and later grout.
functions: Define the tendon path
Separate strands from fresh concrete during casting
Contain tendon grout after stressing

cad.pattern: Continuous supported curve between anchorage trumpets
cad.placement: Within concrete cover and reinforcement envelope
cad.opening: Duct bore remains clear until strands and grout occupy it

notes: Empty, strand-loaded and fully grouted are separate construction states of the same duct.

objects.name: round post-tensioning duct
objects.definition: A post-tensioning duct with an approximately circular cross-section used for a selected bonded tendon strand bundle.
functions: Contain a multi-strand bundle
Provide a grout passage
Follow a three-dimensional tendon profile

cad.pattern: Circular-section continuous curved run
cad.placement: Within beams, slabs or other prestressed members
cad.opening: Internal strand and grout space remains explicit

notes: Diameter is system-selected from strand count, grout access and geometry, not a universal default.

objects.name: flat post-tensioning duct
objects.definition: A low-depth wide duct used to contain a selected number of prestressing strands within thin slabs or other constrained concrete zones.
functions: Fit bonded strands within limited member depth
Define a wide low-profile tendon path
Contain grout around the strands
materials: corrugated metal or plastic flat duct

cad.pattern: Low-profile curved or banded runs
cad.placement: Within slab depth between reinforcement layers
cad.opening: Wide axis orientation must follow the documented profile

notes: Rotating a flat duct can change cover, grout and bending behaviour; preserve its local orientation along the path.

objects.name: post-tensioning duct grout
objects.definition: A flowable cementitious material pumped into a bonded post-tensioning duct after stressing to fill voids, protect the steel and bond the tendon to the concrete member.
functions: Fill the tendon duct
Protect prestressing steel
Bond strands to the surrounding member after hardening

cad.pattern: Continuous filled volume around strands inside the duct
cad.placement: Within bonded tendon duct after stressing
cad.start: Grout inlet or filled anchorage zone
cad.opening: No unverified voids should be invented as solid grout
cad.load: Bond and protection material after verified grouting

notes: Only mark a duct fully grouted when records support that state; planned grout and verified grout are different data states.

objects.name: live-end post-tensioning anchorage
objects.definition: A post-tensioning anchorage accessible for stressing, where the jack pulls the strand or tendon and wedges or other devices retain the applied force.
functions: Provide the stressing interface
Grip the tensioned strand or tendon
Transfer prestressing force into the concrete anchorage zone

cad.pattern: Discrete anchorages at tendon stressing ends
cad.placement: At accessible member face in a reinforced anchorage zone
