cad.opening: Jack access and later recess closure remain explicit states

notes: Live means stressed from this end; it does not mean exposed permanently after construction.

objects.name: dead-end post-tensioning anchorage
objects.definition: A fixed post-tensioning anchorage installed before or during casting and not used as the active jacking end for the tendon.
functions: Anchor the non-stressing tendon end
Transfer tendon force into the concrete
Provide a fixed end for stressing from the opposite anchorage

cad.pattern: Discrete fixed anchor at selected tendon end
cad.placement: Embedded at or within the concrete member end
cad.opening: No jacking access assumed

notes: A dead end can be fully embedded; do not invent an accessible stressing pocket.

objects.name: post-tensioning anchorage head
objects.definition: The steel head, barrel or casting at a post-tensioning anchorage containing wedge holes or other gripping features and bearing against the anchorage plate or concrete zone.
functions: House the strand-gripping devices
Collect forces from individual strands
Transfer tendon force to the bearing component

cad.pattern: Discrete multi-hole or single-hole head at anchorage
cad.placement: At the tendon end against bearing plate or anchorage casting
cad.opening: Wedge bores remain explicit at detailed scale

notes: Proprietary shapes differ; use a generic envelope only until the selected anchorage is known.

objects.name: post-tensioning anchorage wedge set
objects.definition: A matched set of tapered toothed steel wedges seated around a prestressing strand in an anchorage head to grip the strand after stressing.
functions: Grip a prestressing strand
Seat in the anchorage taper
Retain tendon force after jack release

cad.pattern: Segmented tapered set around each strand
cad.placement: Within anchorage head bore
cad.opening: Central strand passage remains

notes: Wedge seating and condition are evidence states; a cone drawn around strand does not prove force retention.

objects.name: post-tensioning anchorage trumpet
objects.definition: A flared transition fitting connecting a tendon duct to the wider anchorage body while guiding strands and containing grout at the anchorage zone.
functions: Transition from duct to anchorage
Guide the strand fan or bundle
Provide a continuous grout and corrosion-protection enclosure

cad.pattern: Flared transition at each bonded tendon anchorage
cad.placement: Between tendon duct and anchorage head or casting
cad.opening: Internal strand and grout passage remains continuous
cad.load: Guide and enclosure, not the primary gripping device

notes: The trumpet must be modelled as part of the protected tendon envelope, not filled with concrete.

objects.name: post-tensioning tendon coupler
objects.definition: A purpose-designed connector joining prestressing tendon lengths or allowing a later tendon stage to continue from an earlier anchored stage.
functions: Continue prestressing force across tendon stages
Join strand groups or anchorage components
Coordinate staged stressing and construction joints

cad.pattern: Discrete enlarged connection on tendon route
cad.placement: At a staged tendon or construction joint location
cad.opening: Coupler envelope and access zone remain clear
cad.load: Prestressing continuity only with selected qualified system

notes: A duct splice joins enclosures; a tendon coupler transfers prestressing force and is not the same object.

objects.name: post-tensioning grout inlet
objects.definition: A small connected port and tube through which grout is introduced into a bonded post-tensioning duct.
functions: Provide a controlled grout entry point
Connect pumping equipment to the duct
Allow closure after verified grouting

cad.pattern: Discrete branch tube at low or selected pumping location
cad.placement: Connected to bonded tendon duct and accessible during grouting
cad.opening: Bore remains open until grouting and closure

notes: After grouting the projecting tube may be cut and sealed; retain only the as-built permanent portion.

objects.name: post-tensioning grout vent
objects.definition: A small connected port and tube at a tendon high point, end or other selected location allowing displaced air, water and grout to exit during bonded-tendon grouting.
functions: Vent trapped air and fluid
Indicate grout arrival at selected locations
Allow controlled closure after grouting

cad.pattern: Branch tubes at high points and tendon ends
cad.placement: Connected to bonded tendon duct and brought to an accessible face
cad.opening: Internal passage remains until grouting and closure

notes: Inlet and vent roles can change with grouting direction; store the documented operation and final closure.

objects.name: post-tensioning tendon chair
objects.definition: A purpose-made support holding a post-tensioning duct or monostrand tendon at a designed elevation and profile point before and during concrete placement.
functions: Set tendon profile height
Prevent displacement during concreting
Transfer construction handling to the lower support layer

cad.pattern: Repeated supports at tendon profile control points
cad.placement: Between lower reinforcement or formwork and tendon
cad.opening: Keep duct or sheath undamaged and concrete flow paths open
cad.load: Temporary construction support retained in concrete

notes: Profile coordinates, not generic equal spacing, should drive chair heights.

objects.name: post-tensioning anchorage recess
objects.definition: A formed pocket in the concrete face providing stressing and finishing access around a post-tensioning anchorage.
functions: Provide jack and wedge access
Keep the anchorage behind the final concrete face
Receive later corrosion protection and patch material
materials: later grout cap or repair mortar

cad.pattern: Discrete pocket at live anchorages
cad.placement: At an accessible concrete face around the anchorage
cad.opening: Pocket is open during stressing and later occupied by selected closure material

notes: Preserve open, protected and patched states rather than permanently hiding the anchorage from inspection data.

objects.name: post-tensioning anchorage grout cap
objects.definition: A protective cap or cementitious closure installed over a completed post-tensioning anchorage to isolate steel and close the stressing recess.
functions: Protect anchorage steel
Close the tendon end or recess
Complete the durability and surface interface

cad.pattern: Discrete closure over anchorage
cad.placement: Within or over the anchorage recess after stressing and strand trimming
cad.opening: Fully occupies selected recess without concealing incomplete evidence state

notes: The cap must remain distinct from the load-bearing anchorage hardware it protects.

objects.name: post-tensioning anchorage-zone reinforcement
objects.definition: A concentrated arrangement of ordinary reinforcing bars, spirals, ties or hairpins surrounding a tendon anchorage to distribute local bursting, spalling and splitting actions into the member.
functions: Reinforce the anchorage zone
Distribute concentrated tendon force
Constrain local cracking and splitting where designed

cad.pattern: Dense local cage around each tendon anchorage
cad.placement: Between anchorage bearing face and distributed member reinforcement
cad.opening: Preserve jack, duct, grout and concrete-placement access

notes: Do not generate a generic helix around every anchorage; the selected system and structural design determine the bar topology.

objects.name: prefabricated concrete structural system
objects.definition: A structural or enclosure system assembled from concrete elements cast away from their final position and then transported, lifted, temporarily braced and connected into the building.
functions: Combine manufactured concrete elements
Coordinate transport, erection and final connections
Transfer actions through completed bearings, joints and connections

cad.pattern: Discrete manufactured elements joined at explicit bearings and connection zones
cad.placement: At final building grid after transport and erection
cad.opening: Element openings, lifting recesses and connection pockets remain explicit
cad.load: Final structure only after documented completion of connections and temporary-work release

notes: Manufacture, transport, lifting, braced erection and final in-service states use different supports and actions and must not be collapsed.

objects.name: prefabricated concrete element
objects.definition: A concrete member manufactured away from its final support position and handled as a discrete unit before incorporation into the completed building.
functions: Provide a manufactured concrete member
Accept lifting and transport actions
Connect to bearings and adjoining elements in the final structure
not_synonyms: precast concrete product not intended for buildings automatically

cad.pattern: Discrete tagged manufactured unit
cad.placement: Stored, transported and finally erected at its documented location
cad.opening: All cast openings and recesses belong to the element definition
cad.load: Changes between handling and final structural states

notes: Precast describes manufacture and handling; loadbearing, cladding, wall, beam and floor describe separate roles.

objects.name: solid precast concrete wall panel
objects.definition: A factory- or site-cast solid concrete panel erected vertically as a loadbearing wall, non-loadbearing wall, facade, retaining element or other documented wall role.
functions: Form a wall plane
Carry in-plane or out-of-plane actions where designed
Provide manufactured openings and connection zones

cad.pattern: Repeated discrete wall panels separated by joints
cad.placement: On foundations, beams, corbels or lower panels
cad.opening: Doors, windows, pockets and inserts are manufactured geometry

notes: Tilt-up identifies a particular casting and erection method; it is not an exact synonym for all solid precast wall panels.

objects.name: precast concrete sandwich wall panel
objects.definition: A prefabricated wall panel containing two concrete wythes separated by a thermal-insulation core and connected by purpose-designed ties or connectors.
functions: Combine structure or enclosure with thermal insulation
Connect inner and outer concrete wythes
Form one transportable wall element
not_synonyms: double wall with site-cast core automatically

cad.pattern: Layered panel with concrete-insulation-concrete stack
cad.placement: As an external or internal wall element
cad.opening: Each layer and connector coordinates around openings
cad.load: Composite, partially composite or non-composite only as documented

notes: The two wythes must remain independently selectable; panel thickness alone cannot reveal whether they act compositely.

objects.name: precast sandwich-panel outer wythe
objects.definition: The exterior concrete layer of a precast sandwich wall panel, exposed to weather or forming the outer architectural face.
functions: Form the exterior concrete face
Protect the insulation core
Transfer its self-weight and environmental actions through selected connectors and bearings
materials: surface finish or coating where selected

cad.pattern: Continuous outer concrete layer within each panel
cad.placement: Weather side of insulation core
cad.opening: Returns and reveals coordinate around panel openings

notes: An architectural outer wythe can be non-loadbearing in the building load path while still carrying its own handling and environmental actions.

objects.name: precast sandwich-panel inner wythe
objects.definition: The interior concrete layer of a precast sandwich wall panel, often providing the main bearing or wall-plane role but only as documented by design.
functions: Form the internal concrete face
Support the insulation and outer wythe through connectors
Carry structural wall actions where assigned

cad.pattern: Continuous inner concrete layer within each panel
cad.placement: Building side of insulation core
cad.opening: Opening edges and connection zones remain explicit

notes: The thicker wythe is not automatically structural; store the design role.

objects.name: precast sandwich-panel insulation core
objects.definition: A rigid thermal-insulation layer cast between the two concrete wythes of a prefabricated sandwich wall panel.
functions: Reduce heat flow through the panel field
Separate the concrete wythes
Continue insulation around compatible connector and opening details
materials: mineral insulation or approved core product

cad.pattern: Continuous insulation field divided at panel boundaries and openings
cad.placement: Between inner and outer concrete wythes
cad.opening: Cut around connectors and return at openings as documented
cad.load: Thermal layer; structural role only if product system documents one

notes: Do not infer whole-wall R-value from nominal core thickness without accounting for joints, connectors, edges and openings.

objects.name: precast sandwich-panel wythe connector
objects.definition: A discrete or linear tie passing through the insulation core to connect the inner and outer concrete wythes of a precast sandwich panel.
functions: Transfer selected actions between wythes
Maintain wythe spacing during manufacture and service
Provide composite or non-composite connection behaviour as designed

cad.pattern: Repeated ties through insulation between wythes
cad.placement: At documented panel grid or truss lines
cad.opening: Passes through a local insulation penetration

notes: Connector layout is a structural and thermal input; never populate a generic grid without the selected system.

objects.name: precast concrete column
objects.definition: A prefabricated vertical concrete member manufactured with lifting points and final bearing or connection details before erection into a building frame.
functions: Carry vertical and bending actions in the completed structure
Support precast beams, slabs or walls
Resist handling and erection actions

cad.pattern: Discrete vertical elements at grid points
cad.placement: On foundations or lower precast supports
cad.opening: Connection pockets and sleeves remain explicit
cad.load: Handling and final column roles are separately evidenced

notes: A precast column may be one-storey or multi-storey; split only at real manufactured joints.

objects.name: precast concrete beam
objects.definition: A prefabricated horizontal or sloping concrete member manufactured for lifting, bearing and connection between columns, walls, corbels or other supports.
functions: Span between supports
Carry slabs, walls or other loads
Provide final bearings and erection connections

cad.pattern: Discrete linear units spanning the structural grid
cad.placement: On corbels, columns, walls or other beam supports
cad.opening: Manufactured web openings and inserts remain explicit
cad.load: Handling and final beam roles are separately checked

notes: Profile variants exist because their ledges and webs support different floor and facade interfaces.

objects.name: precast inverted-T beam
objects.definition: A precast beam with a central web and bearing ledges projecting from both sides near its lower edge to support floor units.
functions: Support precast floor units on both sides
Span between columns or walls
Provide a shallow combined beam-and-floor zone

cad.pattern: Linear beam with two continuous support ledges
cad.placement: Between frame supports with floor units bearing from both sides
cad.opening: Ledge interruptions occur only at designed details

notes: The inverted-T name describes section orientation; do not confuse it with the T-shaped floor units it supports.

objects.name: precast L-shaped spandrel beam
objects.definition: A precast edge beam with one projecting lower ledge, often supporting floor units on the building side while forming an external spandrel or facade edge.
functions: Support floor units from one side
Form the building perimeter beam
Carry facade, barrier or edge loads where designed

cad.pattern: Perimeter linear member with one continuous ledge
cad.placement: At floor edge with ledge facing supported units
cad.opening: Facade and drainage penetrations remain designed details
cad.load: Precast edge beam with asymmetric support role

notes: Ledge orientation is critical and must not flip when a component is mirrored.

objects.name: precast solid concrete slab panel
objects.definition: A solid prefabricated concrete plate used as a floor, roof, balcony or platform unit and supported by bearings or connections at its edges or points.
functions: Form part of a structural floor or roof
Span between supports
Receive joints, topping or finishes

cad.pattern: Repeated plate units over supports
cad.placement: On beams, walls, corbels or columns
cad.opening: Manufactured and later approved openings remain explicit

notes: A panel's transport orientation can differ from its final horizontal position; store both states.

objects.name: precast hollowcore floor plank
objects.definition: A long prestressed precast slab unit containing continuous longitudinal voids that reduce self-weight while retaining webs and flanges for structural action.
functions: Span between support lines
Form repeated floor or roof units
Receive joints, grout and structural topping where selected

cad.pattern: Parallel repeated planks with longitudinal cores
cad.placement: Bearing on beams or walls
cad.opening: Cores and webs constrain cutting; only approved holes and notches are modelled

notes: Do not treat hollow cores as free service routes; strand, web, bearing and fire requirements govern penetrations.

objects.name: precast double-tee floor unit
objects.definition: A wide prestressed precast floor or roof unit with two deep longitudinal stems integral with a thinner top flange.
functions: Span long distances as one floor unit
Carry flange actions into two stems
Bear on beams or walls and connect to adjacent units

cad.pattern: Repeated wide units with two parallel stems
cad.placement: Between beam or wall support lines
cad.opening: Flange penetrations and stem notches require approved geometry
cad.load: Prestressed one-way floor or roof unit

notes: Model flange-to-flange connections separately so diaphragm continuity is not inferred from touching edges.

objects.name: precast concrete stair flight
objects.definition: A prefabricated concrete unit containing a run of stair treads and risers, usually with an integral waist or stringer form, erected between landings or supports.
functions: Provide a stair run
Span between landings, walls or beams
Carry pedestrian and barrier actions where designed

cad.pattern: Repeated steps contained in one sloping manufactured unit
cad.placement: Between lower and upper landing supports
cad.opening: Clearances and connection pockets remain explicit

notes: Tread compliance belongs to the completed stair assembly, not merely the precast element fabrication shape.

objects.name: precast concrete stair landing
objects.definition: A prefabricated horizontal concrete platform unit supporting or joining stair flights and bearing on walls, beams, columns or brackets.
functions: Provide a level stair platform
Support stair-flight ends
Transfer stair and pedestrian actions to the building structure

cad.pattern: Discrete horizontal platform between flights
cad.placement: At intermediate or storey stair levels
cad.opening: Shaft clearances and joints remain explicit

notes: A landing may be integral with a flight or a separate element; model the actual manufactured unit boundary.

objects.name: precast concrete balcony panel
objects.definition: A prefabricated concrete platform element projecting outside or beyond the main floor line and connected back to the building structure.
functions: Form an external balcony platform
Carry pedestrian, barrier and finish loads
Coordinate thermal, waterproofing and drainage interfaces

cad.pattern: Discrete external platform units
cad.placement: At facade floor edges on bearings, brackets or designed connectors
cad.opening: Drains, outlets and barrier anchors remain coordinated

notes: Projection does not prove cantilever action; some panels bear on columns or brackets.

objects.name: precast concrete parapet panel
objects.definition: A prefabricated concrete panel erected at a roof, balcony, bridge or floor edge to form a raised perimeter wall or barrier-supporting element.
functions: Form a raised edge wall
Support facade, coping or barrier components
Transfer wind and barrier actions where designed

cad.pattern: Repeated edge panels with vertical joints
cad.placement: At roof, floor or balcony perimeter
cad.opening: Drainage and facade joints remain explicit
cad.load: Edge wall or barrier support only as designed

notes: A parapet panel and a spandrel beam can occupy the same facade band but have different support and load roles.

objects.name: precast concrete connection assembly
objects.definition: The complete bearing and fastening interface joining a prefabricated concrete element to another element or to cast-in-place, steel or masonry structure.
functions: Transfer documented actions between elements
Locate and restrain the precast unit
Accommodate erection tolerance, grout, bearings and movement

cad.pattern: Discrete or linear interface at every precast support and restraint point
cad.placement: Between element and supporting or adjoining structure
cad.opening: Tolerance gaps, grout spaces and movement clearances remain explicit
cad.load: Only the documented connection components and states transfer actions

notes: Contact geometry is not a connection; bolts, welds, dowels, grout and bearings must be separately complete and verified.

objects.name: precast concrete bearing pad
objects.definition: A purpose-made resilient or high-strength pad placed between a precast element and its support to distribute bearing and accommodate selected rotation or irregularity.
functions: Distribute compressive bearing
Separate concrete bearing faces
Accommodate limited rotation or surface variation where selected

cad.pattern: Discrete pads at bearing seats
cad.placement: Between precast element underside and support
cad.opening: Maintain setback and unconfined edge geometry

notes: A visually similar rubber sheet may not be a structural bearing product; keep product evidence attached.

objects.name: precast concrete grout bed
objects.definition: A placed cementitious or resin grout layer filling the designed gap beneath or behind a precast element to provide continuous bearing and transfer selected compressive actions.
functions: Fill erection tolerance gap
Provide uniform bearing
Transfer compression to the support

cad.pattern: Continuous filled layer over bearing footprint
cad.placement: Between precast base or bearing and support
cad.opening: Exclude drainage, movement or designed void zones
cad.load: Compression transfer only after required cure

notes: Planned grout, placed grout and cured verified grout are different construction states.

objects.name: cast-in precast lifting anchor
objects.definition: A purpose-designed anchor cast into a prefabricated concrete element to engage temporary lifting equipment during demoulding, transport or erection.
functions: Connect lifting equipment to the element
Transfer handling actions into the concrete
Provide a controlled reusable or one-use lifting point
materials: steel or stainless steel lifting anchor

cad.pattern: Discrete lifting points positioned about element centre of gravity
cad.placement: Embedded near an accessible element face
cad.opening: Recess remains open during handling and may be patched later
cad.load: Temporary handling anchor only for documented stages

notes: The anchor may remain cast in, but that does not make it a final building connection.

objects.name: precast lifting clutch
objects.definition: A removable lifting device matched to a cast-in anchor and connected to crane rigging while a precast element is lifted.
functions: Engage the cast-in lifting anchor
Connect the element to lifting rigging
Release after the lift is complete
materials: forged or cast steel lifting device

cad.pattern: Temporary device at active lifting points
cad.placement: Engaged with lifting anchor only during rigging and lifting
cad.opening: Removed before recess closure

notes: Exclude the clutch from completed-building geometry; retain it in erection simulations and lift records only.

objects.name: cast-in precast brace insert
objects.definition: A purpose-designed cast-in insert used to connect a temporary erection brace to a prefabricated concrete panel or other element.
functions: Anchor a temporary brace to the precast element
Transfer erection-stage brace actions
Permit brace removal after final stability is achieved

cad.pattern: Discrete inserts at designed brace connection points
cad.placement: Within the precast element face
cad.opening: Accessible during bracing and patched or capped after removal

notes: The insert can remain physically embedded after the brace is removed; its lifecycle role remains temporary bracing.

objects.name: precast panel temporary brace
objects.definition: An adjustable diagonal strut connecting an erected precast panel to a designed foundation, slab or brace footing until final structural stability is complete.
functions: Stabilise the panel during erection
Resist construction wind and incidental actions
Maintain plumb and alignment until release

cad.pattern: Usually paired diagonal braces per panel or as designed
cad.placement: From panel brace inserts to verified foot anchors
cad.opening: Maintain access and exclusion zones

notes: Brace count, angle, capacity, anchors and release timing require a bracing design; geometry tools must not invent them.

objects.name: precast insert recess patch
objects.definition: A compatible mortar, grout or proprietary plug installed after lifting or brace hardware is removed to close and protect the remaining recess in a precast element.
functions: Close the insert recess
Protect retained embedded steel
Restore the selected surface profile and exposure protection

cad.pattern: Discrete closures at former lifting or brace recesses
cad.placement: Flush or profiled with the finished precast face
cad.opening: Occupies the recess only after hardware removal
cad.load: Protective closure unless explicitly designed otherwise

notes: The patch does not erase the as-built insert record or permit the lifting point to be reused automatically.

objects.name: concrete formwork and falsework system
objects.definition: The temporary mould, supporting members, ties, braces, shores and foundations that contain fresh concrete and carry construction actions until the concrete can support the required stage.
functions: Shape and contain fresh concrete
Support wet concrete, reinforcement and construction loads
Transfer temporary actions safely to verified supports

cad.pattern: Load path from concrete face through sheathing, joists, bearers, shores, braces and foundations
cad.placement: Around and beneath the future concrete member
cad.end: Verified temporary-work foundation or supporting structure
cad.opening: Access, penetrations, clean-outs and pour openings remain explicit
cad.load: Temporary works; capacity and stability require design evidence

notes: A SketchUp model can document geometry and sequence but must never label formwork safe from shape alone.

objects.name: concrete form face
objects.definition: The sheathing or panel surface directly contacting fresh concrete and defining the formed shape, joint pattern and surface texture after stripping.
functions: Contain fresh concrete
Create the designed concrete face
Transfer pressure to studs, joists, walers or frames

cad.pattern: Tiled panels following the future concrete surface
cad.placement: Immediately outside the concrete volume
cad.opening: Cut around ties, cast-ins, clean-outs and blockouts

notes: The form face is removed unless explicitly documented as permanent formwork; the off-form concrete face remains.

objects.name: formwork plywood panel
objects.definition: A structural plywood sheet manufactured and finished specifically for use as concrete form sheathing and selected off-form surface quality.
functions: Provide a continuous concrete contact face
Span between formwork supports
Permit controlled reuse when condition remains suitable

cad.pattern: Rectangular sheets tiled over joists, studs or modular frames
cad.placement: As the concrete contact sheathing
cad.opening: Cutouts require supported and sealed edges
cad.load: Temporary sheathing spanning to form supports

notes: Surface grade, stress grade and remaining reuse condition are separate properties.

objects.name: steel concrete form panel
objects.definition: A reusable framed steel panel providing a rigid concrete contact face for walls, columns, beams, edges or repetitive precast work.
functions: Contain fresh concrete
Provide a durable repeatable mould face
Transfer pressure through panel frames, ties and braces

cad.pattern: Repeated modular panels connected edge-to-edge
cad.placement: Against the future concrete face
cad.opening: Tie and cast-in penetrations occur at documented locations

notes: A steel form panel is temporary equipment even when used to manufacture permanent precast panels.

objects.name: concrete wall formwork assembly
objects.definition: Opposing or one-sided form faces, frames, ties, walers, braces and supports arranged to cast a concrete wall.
functions: Define wall thickness and faces
Resist fresh-concrete pressure
Hold cast-ins, openings and reinforcement interfaces

cad.pattern: Paired or single form faces along wall route
cad.placement: Around wall reinforcement and concrete volume
cad.opening: Boxouts, cast-ins and clean-outs remain explicit

notes: One-sided wall forms need a different restraint topology from tied opposing shutters.

objects.name: concrete column formwork assembly
objects.definition: A closed set of form faces, yokes, clamps, ties and braces arranged around a column reinforcement cage to contain the column pour.
functions: Define column cross-section and alignment
Resist fresh-concrete pressure
Hold corners, chamfers and cast-ins
materials: plywood, timber, steel or proprietary column forms

cad.pattern: Closed form perimeter around column axis
cad.placement: Outside column cage from base to pour top
cad.opening: Base clean-out and beam intersections remain coordinated

notes: Circular tubes, modular steel forms and site-built box forms are variants with different joints and removal states.

objects.name: suspended slab formwork assembly
objects.definition: A horizontal form face supported by joists, bearers, props, frames or falsework to carry reinforcement, fresh concrete and construction actions for a suspended slab.
functions: Define slab soffit and edges
Carry wet-concrete and construction loads
Transfer temporary actions to verified supports

cad.pattern: Layered support grid below the future slab
cad.placement: Between slab soffit and temporary-work foundations
cad.opening: Shaft and penetration forms have trimmed support frames

notes: Stripping the sheathing and retaining backprops creates a different load path and must be a model state, not a visibility toggle only.

objects.name: concrete beam formwork assembly
objects.definition: Beam soffit and side forms with yokes, joists, bearers, props and braces arranged to contain and support a concrete beam pour.
functions: Define beam sides and soffit
Contain fresh-concrete pressure
Support wet beam weight and transfer it to temporary supports

cad.pattern: Linear U-shaped mould with support grid below
cad.placement: Around future beam sides and soffit
cad.opening: Web penetrations and beam-column joints require explicit forms

notes: Beam sides can sometimes strip before the soffit support; retain component-level removal states.

objects.name: concrete edge form
objects.definition: A temporary vertical or sloping board, panel or metal profile defining the free edge of a slab, footing, topping or other concrete placement.
functions: Contain concrete at a free edge
Set edge line, level and profile
Hold rebates, chamfers and cast-ins where selected
not_synonyms: stop-end at a pour joint automatically

cad.pattern: Continuous boundary form following concrete edge
cad.placement: At free edge of the pour
cad.opening: Breaks at planned openings and special profiles

notes: Boxing can mean the whole forming activity in trade speech, so it is not an exact synonym outside edge context.

objects.name: concrete pour stop-end form
objects.definition: A temporary form closing the end of a concrete placement at a construction joint and shaping its face, key, reinforcement penetrations and waterstop interfaces.
functions: Terminate the current pour
Form the construction-joint face
Locate bars, keys and waterstops through the joint
materials: expanded or proprietary stop-end system where selected
not_synonyms: edge form at free edge automatically

cad.pattern: Panel closing full pour cross-section
cad.placement: At a planned construction-joint line
cad.opening: Bars and waterstops pass through sealed openings

notes: The stop-end is removed; the shaped concrete construction joint remains.

objects.name: concrete blockout former
objects.definition: A temporary box, foam shape, tube or framed mould fixed within the formwork to keep concrete out of a planned blockout, opening or recess.
functions: Create an omitted concrete volume
Hold opening shape during placement
Provide removable or sacrificial temporary moulding

cad.pattern: Discrete negative mould inside the concrete boundary
cad.placement: At the future blockout or recess
cad.opening: Former occupies the future void during pouring

notes: The former and the resulting opening must not coexist as overlapping permanent solids.

objects.name: formwork joist
objects.definition: A repeated secondary temporary member directly supporting slab or beam form sheathing and spanning to bearers, frames or primary supports.
functions: Support form sheathing
Transfer wet-concrete and construction loads to bearers
Control sheathing span and deflection

cad.pattern: Repeated parallel secondary members beneath sheathing
cad.placement: Between form face and bearers
cad.opening: Trim around formwork openings with designed support

notes: Joist and bearer naming depends on hierarchy; store what each member directly supports.

objects.name: formwork bearer
objects.definition: A primary horizontal temporary member supporting formwork joists or panels and transferring their loads to props, frames, shores or falsework towers.
functions: Support secondary joists or panels
Collect formwork loads
Transfer temporary actions to vertical supports

cad.pattern: Repeated primary members crossing below joists
cad.placement: Between joists and props or frames
cad.opening: Support discontinuities require designed transfer members

notes: Bearer reactions must land on verified heads or frames; visual intersection with a prop is not proof of bearing.

objects.name: formwork waler
objects.definition: A horizontal or otherwise transverse member outside wall or column form panels that collects pressure reactions and transfers them to ties, soldiers or braces.
functions: Align and stiffen form panels
Collect fresh-concrete pressure
Distribute reactions to ties and primary frames

cad.pattern: Repeated continuous runs outside vertical form panels
cad.placement: Across studs, frames or panel backs
cad.opening: Tie and bracket positions remain explicit

notes: Waler orientation can vary in proprietary systems; its support function is more reliable than the word horizontal.

objects.name: formwork soldier
objects.definition: A strong primary vertical or inclined member behind wall formwork that supports walers or panels and transfers pressure reactions to ties, braces or foundations.
functions: Stiffen vertical formwork
Collect reactions from panels or walers
Transfer actions to ties and braces

cad.pattern: Repeated primary verticals behind wall form
cad.placement: Outside panel backs or walers
cad.opening: Coordinate access platforms and ties

notes: Strongback can also mean a local stiffener on precast or timber work, so it is related rather than exact.

objects.name: adjustable formwork prop
objects.definition: A telescopic or screw-adjustable vertical temporary support carrying formwork bearers, beams or slabs to a verified supporting surface.
functions: Support formwork vertically
Adjust level and preload within the designed procedure
Transfer construction actions to the support below

cad.pattern: Repeated vertical supports under bearers or beams
cad.placement: Between formwork head and verified base support
cad.opening: Bracing and access zones remain clear
cad.load: Temporary compression support with rated extension range

notes: Acrow is proprietary-derived trade usage; the canonical term remains adjustable prop.

objects.name: formwork head jack
objects.definition: An adjustable screw head, fork head or drop head fitted at the top of a prop or falsework frame to support and level a bearer or panel system.
functions: Adjust top level
Provide a centred bearing or fork restraint
Allow selected early-striking or drop-head sequence where designed

cad.pattern: One head at each prop or frame support point
cad.placement: Between vertical support and bearer or panel
cad.opening: Fork clearance and centred bearing remain explicit

notes: Extension limits and eccentricity are design inputs; do not stretch a generic jack to fit arbitrary geometry.

objects.name: formwork base jack
objects.definition: An adjustable screw base fitted beneath a falsework frame, shore or support tower to level it and transfer compression into a soleplate or verified foundation.
functions: Adjust base level
Provide a bearing plate
Transfer vertical actions into the supporting foundation

cad.pattern: One base at each falsework leg
cad.placement: Between vertical frame and soleplate or foundation
cad.opening: Maintain full plate bearing and drainage conditions

notes: Loose bricks or uncontrolled packing are not modelled as equivalent base jacks.

objects.name: formwork brace
objects.definition: A diagonal or horizontal temporary member restraining formwork, props or falsework against sway, overturning, racking or loss of alignment.
functions: Stabilise temporary works
Transfer lateral actions to verified anchor points
Maintain line, level and plumb during construction

cad.pattern: Triangulated or repeated restraint lines
cad.placement: Between formwork frames and verified anchors or between falsework bays
cad.opening: Maintain access without deleting required stability paths

notes: The generator must not omit braces to simplify geometry; any brace layout requires actual temporary-works design.

objects.name: concrete wall form tie rod
objects.definition: A tension rod or proprietary tie passing through or between opposing wall forms to hold their separation and resist fresh-concrete pressure.
functions: Tie opposing form faces together
Maintain wall thickness with spacers or cones
Transfer pressure reactions to walers and anchor nuts

cad.pattern: Repeated ties crossing between opposing forms
cad.placement: Through sleeves or cones across wall thickness
cad.opening: Tie hole remains after removable parts are extracted and requires documented closure

notes: Model removable rod, retained sleeve and later tie-hole patch as separate lifecycle parts.

objects.name: form tie cone
objects.definition: A tapered fitting at a wall-form tie end that sets cover or wall-face geometry and creates a recess for tie removal and later patching.
functions: Position the tie relative to the concrete face
Prevent concrete locking selected removable tie parts
Form a controlled tie-hole recess

cad.pattern: Paired cones at wall tie locations
cad.placement: Between tie sleeve and form face
cad.opening: Creates a tapered recess after removal

notes: A tie cone is not a waterproof closure; a separate plug, patch or waterstop detail may follow.

objects.name: form tie spacer tube
objects.definition: A tube surrounding a form tie through the wall thickness to maintain form separation, isolate a removable rod from concrete and leave a controlled tie hole.
functions: Set wall thickness
Keep concrete off a removable tie rod
Create a predictable hole for later closure

cad.pattern: Repeated tubes across wall thickness
cad.placement: Between opposing tie cones or form faces
cad.opening: Internal bore remains after rod removal until closed
cad.load: Thickness spacer and rod sleeve, not structural reinforcement

notes: The retained tube and its closure can create leakage or fire paths if omitted from the as-built model.

objects.name: table form assembly
objects.definition: A large reusable slab-form module combining a deck, joists, bearers and supporting frames or props so the unit can be moved between repeated floor bays.
functions: Form a large slab soffit area
Move as a reusable module
Support repeated floor construction cycles

cad.pattern: Large repeated deck modules spanning one or more bays
cad.placement: Below suspended slabs and moved floor-to-floor
cad.opening: Building edges, shafts and moving clearances remain explicit

notes: Flying describes how a table is moved; not every table form is crane-flown.

objects.name: jump-form assembly
objects.definition: A vertical formwork, platform and support assembly repositioned in discrete lifts to cast successive wall or core sections.
functions: Cast repeated vertical lifts
Carry form panels, platforms and access
Reposition to the next completed support level

cad.pattern: Vertical module repeated at discrete lift levels
cad.placement: Attached to completed wall or core below the active pour
cad.opening: Shafts, door openings and anchor recesses coordinate with each jump

notes: Jump form moves intermittently; slip form moves continuously or near-continuously during placement.

objects.name: slip-form assembly
objects.definition: A short-height form, yoke, jack and platform assembly that moves progressively while concrete is placed to create a continuous vertical or other uniform section.
functions: Form continuous concrete with moving shutters
Support work platforms and reinforcement placement
Maintain section geometry during controlled movement

cad.pattern: Short moving form ring or pair around a continuous pour
cad.placement: At the active concrete setting zone
cad.opening: Embedded items and openings require timed inserts and blockouts

notes: Slip-form geometry is inseparable from time and concrete-set state; a static extrusion alone is not an erection plan.

objects.name: concrete falsework assembly
objects.definition: A temporary loadbearing structure of frames, towers, shores, beams, braces and foundations supporting formwork or incomplete concrete until the permanent structure can carry the required stage.
functions: Carry formwork and construction actions
Bridge to suitable temporary-work foundations
Provide stable vertical and lateral load paths during construction

cad.pattern: Three-dimensional temporary support frame below or beside formwork
cad.placement: Between formwork loads and verified ground or permanent supports
cad.opening: Access bays and service routes cannot remove required bracing

notes: Formwork is the mould; falsework is the supporting temporary structure. They overlap as systems but are not synonyms.

objects.name: concrete slab backprop
objects.definition: A temporary vertical support installed or retained beneath a concrete slab after some primary formwork is removed to carry construction-stage actions through the developing structure.
functions: Support an early-age or loaded slab
Transfer construction actions to lower levels
Maintain a staged load path during formwork cycling

cad.pattern: Repeated vertical props through selected levels
cad.placement: Below a stripped or partly stripped concrete slab
cad.opening: Prop grid coordinates with access and lower slab capacity

notes: Backpropping changes load distribution between floors and needs an engineered sequence, not a copied prop grid.

objects.name: concrete form release agent film
objects.definition: A thin temporary treatment applied to a form face to reduce adhesion between the hardened concrete and the form during stripping.
functions: Assist clean form removal
Limit damage to concrete and form face
Support the selected formed-surface result when compatible
materials: proprietary release oil, emulsion or chemical release agent

cad.pattern: Microscopic continuous film over concrete-contact face
cad.placement: On the form face before concrete placement
cad.opening: Exclude reinforcement and construction-joint faces unless product and method allow

notes: Do not retain release agent as a permanent visible coating layer on the concrete; residue and compatibility are surface-condition evidence.

objects.name: concrete form liner
objects.definition: A patterned or absorbent sheet fixed to the form face to impart a selected texture, relief or surface effect to formed concrete.
functions: Create a repeated or bespoke concrete texture
Modify the concrete-contact surface
Protect or adapt the reusable base form panel

cad.pattern: Tiled or continuous patterned sheet over base form
cad.placement: Between base form face and fresh concrete
cad.opening: Pattern aligns around ties, joints and corners

notes: The liner is removed; the inverse relief remains as concrete surface geometry or texture data.

objects.name: formwork chamfer strip
objects.definition: A triangular or shaped strip fixed in a form corner to create a chamfer, fillet, drip or other linear profile in the hardened concrete edge.
functions: Shape a concrete edge
Reduce sharp arrises where selected
Create repeated linear grooves or drips

cad.pattern: Continuous strips along selected form corners
cad.placement: At junction of form faces
cad.opening: Miter or form junctions at corners

notes: The strip and the resulting chamfer are opposite geometries; retain only the concrete profile in the completed state.

objects.name: permanent concrete formwork panel
objects.definition: A panel or profiled sheet used to contain fresh concrete and deliberately left as part of the completed building after the concrete hardens.
functions: Act as concrete form during construction
Remain as a soffit, lining, deck or protective layer
Contribute structural, fire, finish or durability roles only where documented

cad.pattern: Panels or profiled sheets spanning between permanent supports
cad.placement: At concrete soffit, face or deck and retained after curing
cad.opening: Penetrations require trimmed and sealed retained edges
cad.load: Construction and final roles must be documented separately

notes: Permanent formwork remains physical geometry, but remaining in place does not automatically make it composite reinforcement or a compliant finish.
